title: Event contract canary and typing prober
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight canary that emits synthetic usage events through the full console ingestion path and a parallel typing prober that validates field-level types and soft-failure semantics. Purpose: detect contract drift early, measure how downstream enrichers/consumers react to unexpected shapes, and provide deterministic signals for rollout gating before schema changes reach production. This work sits alongside existing intake backpressure and schema reconciliation efforts but targets active drift detection and safe tolerant behavior (soft-fail / quarantine) rather than bulk migration or hard validation.
acceptance_criteria: A deployable canary job that emits 3 configurable event archetypes (minimal, extended with optional fields, and deprecated-shape) to the console event pipeline on a schedule
Typing prober service that pulls events from the nearline topic, runs type assertions against current contract spec, and emits a compact drift report to the telemetry dashboard
Quarantine flagging flow implemented: events failing critical assertions are tagged and routed to a quarantine topic instead of being rejected outright
Alerting rules and a runbook created: significant drift >1% of traffic for 15m opens a P1 page and creates a ticket template for owners
End-to-end test (CI) that validates canary emission, prober detection, and quarantine routing in an ephemeral environment
comments: 2026-02-26 Aisha Patel: Filed initial ticket after postmortem discussion — goal is early detection of contract drift without blocking user traffic. Sketch attached in Confluence (link below).

2026-03-01 Diego Moreno: Spike complete. Implemented a minimal canary prototype that emits to the test topic and a PoC prober that validates types using relaxed casting rules. Observed three common drift patterns in staging: optional-field promotion, integer/string coercion, and missing nested arrays. Detailed notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Event+Canary+Spike

2026-03-03 Engineering review: Decided to implement quarantine topic and a low-latency prober that processes a sample stream rather than full traffic to keep costs down. Trade-offs: sampling increases detection latency but reduces cost and noise. Recording decision here.

2026-03-05 Design review (PM): PM asks for a small dashboard tile summarizing the last 24h drift by contract and suggested owner. Agreed to add a webhook to create issues when a new contract owner is detected as missing.

2026-03-07 Diego Moreno: Draft PR opened for canary emitter and prober infra: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-telemetry/pull/482. Integration tests failing due to IAM scope for quarantine topic; working with infra to get a short-lived role for CI.

2026-03-09 SRE note: Need to ensure canary won't consume Dedicated capacity — added rate limit to emitter (1 req/min by default) and a runtime flag to throttle to zero in emergencies. Added to runbook.
notes: This ticket intentionally errs on the side of permissive typing for non-critical fields and focuses hard assertions only on fields that downstream billing and compliance rely on. If the prober detects repeated hard-assertion failures, follow-up ticket will move those assertions into the intake contract enforcement pipeline.
